To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) spatial data with complex semantics are more coherent than data with only simple semantics and 2) the spatial coherence of data is higher than the temporal coherence.
the semantic structure of the data is crucial to the success of automatic integration processes and that the spatio- semantic coherence of the data is a key factor for successful integration.
the integration of 3D models is not only a geometrical task, but also a semantic one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for the integration of distributed 3D city data, which is a crucial step towards 3D spatial data infrastructures.
the development of methods for automatic integration of complex 3D city data.
the integration of distributed 3D data with complex semantics and the analysis of the spatio- semantic coherence of these data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic information of 3D data can be exploited for the integration process, if it is spatially coherent with the geometry.
the more the spatial data is coherent with respect to the spatial and thematic structure, the easier it is to integrate the data.
the more the spatial data is structured semantically and the more the semantic information is structured spatially, the better the integration process can be supported.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3D data with complex semantics are a promising approach to improve the integration quality and the integration speed.
the semantic structure of the data is a key factor in the integration process.
the integration process is strongly influenced by the quality of the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spatially fragmented data with complex semantics can be integrated more easily than spatially coherent data with simple semantics.
the semantic structure is as important for the integration process of 3D geospatial data as the geometry.
the semantic information of 3D geospatial data is not only a valuable resource for applications, but can also help to improve the quality of data integration.
